clue.text: Put in religious calendar, soon is accepted by church

indicators.note: something accepted by a body is taken in, so the church letters enclose the rest

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
anon is an old word for soon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A saint is about to be added to the calendar, the church agreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soon is' looks like plain surface English but splits into a synonym for soon plus IS; CE (Church of England) is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Declaring someone a saint gives them a feast day in the Church's calendar.

clue.text: Piece of news that's also out of date

explanation.surface: A news story that is stale.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is Latin-derived and archaic, hence 'out of date'.
explanation.definitionFit: A news report is a single story in a paper; and the old adverb meaning likewise, from Latin, is now obsolete.

clue.text: Garment covering shoulders and head

explanation.surface: Clothing that covers both shoulders and head.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless cloak worn over the shoulders; and a headland jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Managed to board and captured

explanation.surface: Someone got onto a vehicle and was then arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: You get on a train or bus you reach in time; and a seized criminal has been taken.

clue.text: Harvests displayed in shelving at her supermarket

indicators.note: the letters are on show inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Produce is laid out on the shelves of her local supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed in' points to the run inside shelvinG AT HER SUPermarket.
explanation.definitionFit: To harvest is to collect crops in, as a verb phrase meaning to collect together.

clue.text: Ego-involved a lot about chapter that's dottily prophetic

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the preceding word are jumbled
about means surrounding, so the word for a lot goes round the chapter letter

parts.note: many means a lot

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed book chapter that predicts the future rather eccentrically.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Ego-involved' disguises the anagram signal; geomancy divines from patterns of dots, hence 'dottily'.
explanation.definitionFit: This divination reads figures made of dots or marks on the ground to foretell events.

clue.text: Immature, played with digits, showing growing ability

parts.note: green means inexperienced or unripe
fingered means handled or played with the fingers

explanation.surface: A naive person fiddled with their fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled at gardening is said to have green fingers, a talent for getting plants to grow.

clue.text: Maximum speed in ordinary bus, oddly, remains most vague

indicators.note: in places the speed letter inside the jumbled letters of the vehicle word
oddly means strangely arranged, so the letters of the word bus are mixed up

parts.note: c is the physicists' symbol for the speed of light, the greatest possible speed
rest means what remains

explanation.surface: A bus driver hits top speed while the remaining passengers are bemused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' jumbles BUS into BSU and 'in' puts C inside it, giving BSCU. 'Maximum speed' is c, the speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of obscure, meaning least clear or most unclear.

clue.text: Irons, for example, a suit

explanation.surface: Golf equipment and playing cards side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are golf sticks used to hit the ball; and one of the four card suits, marked with trefoils.

clue.text: Infinitely deep Shakespearean role? Not so

parts.note: Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Is a famous Shakespeare part endlessly profound? Apparently not.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no base goes down forever, unfathomable.

clue.text: Birds exhibited in Science Museum

indicators.note: the letters are on display within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Stuffed birds on show at the Science Museum in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Large flightless Australian runners, an example of the category.

clue.text: One female in partnership

parts.note: a woman who is half of a married couple

explanation.definitionFit: A married woman is one of the two partners in a marriage.

clue.text: What's circled in 18 Across could stand for such a long time

definitions.text: What's circled in 18 Across could stand for such a long time

parts.words: What's circled in 18 Across could stand for such a long time
parts.note: the symbol for publishing rights is a letter in a ring, and that letter abbreviates periods of a hundred years

explanation.walkthrough: 18 Across is COPYRIGHT, whose symbol is a C in a circle; C can abbreviate a hundred-year span.
explanation.definitionFit: Hundreds of years are a very long time, and C is their abbreviation.

clue.text: Chart is a dreadfully old way to show financial position

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests the preceding words are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A chart that clumsily presents a company's finances in an outdated style.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank's proportion of liquid funds to deposits is a measure of its financial standing.

clue.text: Transient, changing immediately

indicators.note: changing means the letters of the previous word alter their order

explanation.surface: Something fleeting alters at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A rather formal adverb meaning at once, without delay.

clue.text: Vast quantities of 3 and 4 briefly reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the letters are to be said out loud

parts.note: 3 Down abbreviated is C, as is 4 Across (C for caught in cricket), so together two Cs

explanation.surface: Huge amounts of two earlier answers, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 Down is CAPE and 4 Across CAUGHT; each is shortened to C (C for cape on maps, c for caught on cricket scorecards). Two Cs spoken sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: We speak of seas of faces or of mud, meaning great expanses or amounts.

clue.text: Appropriate characters standing for 8 and 21, say

indicators.note: say means the letters are spoken out loud

parts.note: 8 Down and 21 Down are each abbreviated C (C for clubs in cards, C for cold on taps), so two Cs

explanation.surface: Fitting symbols represent two other answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is a verb here, not the adjective it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take for oneself, grab.

clue.text: Remarks heard from down and

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Remarks heard from down and (4)': it ends after 'and', apparently cut short, and no scan or web search gives the rest.

clue.text: Part of aircraft that provides lift over Atlantic

explanation.surface: The bit of a plane that helps it climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged tailplane surface controlling pitch; and the American word, across the ocean, for a passenger hoist in a building.

clue.text: Control over published material, page included by modest author, say

indicators.note: included by means the page letter sits inside the word for modest

parts.note: coy means modest or shy

indicators.note: say means the word for author, as a verb, is spoken out loud

parts.note: to author is to write

explanation.surface: A retiring writer guards their published work, even a single page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'author' is a verb, to write; spoken, it sounds like RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal right to control reproduction of a published work.

clue.text: Origins of crosswords in rebuses, conundrums, and acrostics, roughly speaking

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Crosswords arose roughly from rebuses, riddles and acrostics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Origins of' takes the initials of the five following words.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin preposition meaning approximately, used with dates.

clue.text: Support a Yankee, for example

parts.note: a Yankee is a type of accumulator bet on four horses

explanation.surface: Backing an American.
explanation.walkthrough: A Yankee is a British betting term: eleven bets on four selections.
explanation.definitionFit: To help or encourage someone, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Mugger, for one, doesn't finish off feeble old person

indicators.note: the word loses its finishing letter, so the last one goes

parts.note: a crock is an old and decrepit person

explanation.surface: A street robber doesn't quite kill off a frail pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: The mugger is a species of Indian crocodile, not a robber.
explanation.definitionFit: The mugger is a crocodile, for which this is the short form.

clue.text: Conservative outdated? That's a common complaint

parts.note: old means outdated

explanation.surface: Is the Conservative party old-fashioned? A frequent grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday viral infection is the most widespread ailment.

clue.text: Gold found in river with one other metal — very heavy

indicators.note: found in means the gold word is located inside the river

parts.note: the Trent is a river in the English Midlands
or is gold in heraldry
I is the Roman numeral one
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Gold panned from a river alongside another metal.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is heraldic gold and the Trent is a river in the English Midlands; 'very heavy' describes rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrential rain falls in floods, so the word describes a very heavy downpour.

clue.text: A head some teachers selected

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A head teacher chosen from a group of staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Per head and apiece mean the same: for every individual.

clue.text: Coerce, in a way, following protest

indicators.note: following means the word for way comes after the word for protest

parts.note: to rail is to protest loudly
a road is a way

explanation.surface: Being forced into something after making a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To force someone into acting hastily, pushed through as on a track.

clue.text: Diamonds, for example, that can be useful when dating

definitions.text: that can be useful when dating

explanation.surface: Gems are useful on a romantic date.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds are a crystal form of this element; and radiocarbon decay is used to estimate the age of remains.
